clue.text: Using a ruse or otherwise he'll cause a stir

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged in a different way, so the letters of the preceding words are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A schemer stirs up trouble by means of a cunning trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' signals the rearrangement; the cunning trick of the surface matters only for its letters, and 'Using' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rouses others, stirring up feeling, is one who causes a commotion.

clue.text: Nowadays the wealthy individual keeps it as extras

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

indicators.note: keeps means the rich man holds the next word inside him

parts.note: Dives is the rich man in the parable of Lazarus
taken as written

explanation.surface: These days a rich person treats something as surplus.
explanation.walkthrough: Dives (Latin for rich man) is the name given to the rich man in Luke's parable; 'keeps' puts IT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Additives are substances put into food or fuel in addition, so extras.

clue.text: Assessment of work on the occiput

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: op., opus, is a musical work
the inion is the bony bump at the back of the skull, on the occiput

explanation.surface: An evaluation of a surgical operation on the back of the head.
explanation.walkthrough: The inion is the anatomical name for the external point on the back of the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a judgment or view one forms, so an evaluation.

clue.text: Agree with the children in a minor matter

parts.note: to side with someone is to agree with them
issue means offspring, as in 'died without issue'

explanation.surface: Go along with the kids on something unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: A side issue is a point of secondary importance, off the main question.

clue.text: Incline to strike about the first of May

indicators.note: about means the striking word goes round the letter taken from May

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply

indicators.note: the first of picks out only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A tendency to go on strike at the start of May Day.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is a sloping surface, so an incline.

clue.text: Turner excels. Brown is behind

indicators.note: the brown piece comes after the excelling piece, sitting behind it in the answer

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo or excel it
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Praise for J.M.W. Turner as a painter, with a rival named Brown trailing him.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised Turner suggests the painter, but the definition means anything that turns: a ship's winch for hauling cable.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a rotating drum on a ship, wound round to haul in a cable, so it is a thing that turns.

clue.text: Write letters to arrange match

explanation.surface: Exchanging letters to set up a fixture or a pairing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to arrange' is padding joining the two senses; the surface suggests pen-pals fixing a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To correspond is to exchange letters; things that correspond agree or tally, so match.

clue.text: Post soft flimsy stuff

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
lace is delicate open fabric

explanation.surface: Mailing some delicate fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' suggests mail, but here it means to station or put someone somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To post a sentry is to station or position them.

clue.text: After the examination made a meal with a will

indicators.note: after means the eating piece comes following the examination

parts.note: a test is an examination
ate means dined, made a meal

explanation.surface: Having lunch after an exam, eagerly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a will' sounds like eagerly, but it means having left a legal will.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies testate has made a valid legal will.

clue.text: A pensioner very often shows courage

indicators.note: shows means the letters are on display within the words that follow 'A'

explanation.surface: An elderly retiree frequently displays bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' displays the run spanning 'pensioner very'; 'often' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: To have nerve is to have boldness or daring.

clue.text: The doctor that's departed forgot his past

parts.note: Dr is the usual abbreviation for doctor
that is, abbreviated i.e.
d. is the abbreviation for died, used of the departed in genealogies

explanation.surface: A doctor who has died and left his own history behind.
explanation.walkthrough: An actor who dries forgets his lines; the printed 'past' is probably a misprint for 'part', which is what makes the definition fit.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre slang to dry is to forget one's lines on stage, so a performer who dried lost his part.

clue.text: Combine receiving a short answer — the bird!

indicators.note: receiving means the merger takes in the abbreviation, holding it within

parts.note: a combine, a joining of firms, is a merger
ans. is a shortened form of answer

explanation.surface: A business merger accepts a curt reply, and then someone exclaims at a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The merganser is a fish-eating diving duck with a serrated bill.

clue.text: A dim-witted person about fifty-one really dim

indicators.note: about means the fool's word goes round the numerals, enclosing them

parts.note: a twit is a foolish person
in Roman numerals L is fifty and I is one

explanation.surface: Someone slow-witted, around fifty-one years old, is very dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dim' appears twice: in the person it means stupid, in the definition it means poorly lit, as at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilit describes the half-light of dusk, so something lit only faintly.

clue.text: Prizing for example a merry… party on retirement

indicators.note: retirement is withdrawing, going backwards, so the whole run of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: a revel is a lively celebration

explanation.surface: A jolly celebration given for someone leaving work, prized as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on retirement' reverses EG + A + REVEL as one run, giving LEVER A GE. 'Prizing' is from prise, levering open, not from prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Prizing a lid open uses a lever, and leverage is the action or advantage of using one.

clue.text: Treat no man badly over the range

indicators.note: badly means put in poor order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cruel handling of anyone across the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges TREATNOMAN; the answer is also a cold north wind off the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramontane is from the Italian for beyond the mountains, so describes what lies on the far side of a range.

clue.text: "And pair their rhymes as yokes her doves" (Byron)

definitions.text: "And pair their rhymes as yokes her doves" (Byron)

parts.words: "And pair their rhymes as yokes her doves" (Byron)
parts.note: a line from Byron's English Bards and Scotch Reviewers with a goddess's name missing; she drives a chariot drawn by doves

explanation.walkthrough: The printed line has a gap where a name belongs; the goddess of love traditionally rides a chariot pulled by a pair of doves.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical myth the Roman goddess of love is drawn by doves, so she is the one who yokes them.

clue.text: They write about beers

parts.note: re means concerning or about
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Journalists produce articles on the subject of ales.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists who file news stories are people whose job is writing.

clue.text: Dash up with relation for an explanation

parts.note: a ratio is a proportional relation between quantities

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: élan means dash or flair

explanation.surface: Rushing upwards with a family member to give a reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ELAN to NALE. 'relation' looks like a relative, but it is a ratio.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning behind something, so an account of why.

clue.text: It's essential to keep stocking up

definitions.text: It's essential to keep stocking up

parts.words: It's essential to keep stocking up
parts.note: reads like shop restocking, but means a garter clip that holds a stocking up on the leg

explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking up' looks like laying in supplies; it is a stocking being held up.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap with a clip that holds up a stocking or sock is indispensable for keeping it in place.

clue.text: Means test organised by government officials

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ministers set up an inquiry into whether claimants need benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: A means test is the British check on income before paying state benefit; 'organised' rearranges its nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior political figures who run the affairs of state are leading figures in government.

clue.text: Ways military personnel used up the store of ammunition

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the whole run of pieces reads from bottom to top

parts.note: lanes are roads or ways
RA, the Royal Artillery, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Gunners exhausted their supplies, using up roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LANES + RA as one run; 'used' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a place where weapons and munitions are stored.

clue.text: You take ages to read the newspaper!

explanation.surface: A jibe at a slow reader who dawdles over the daily paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads as teasing, but 'ages' and the paper's own name are the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages, long periods, are also times; and The Times is the newspaper printing this puzzle.

clue.text: Having obliged about five hundred, the good man is most resentful

indicators.note: about means the obliging word goes round the numeral

parts.note: made, as in 'made him do it', means obliged
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
St, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: Forced to deal with five hundred, a decent man is furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad here means angry, so the superlative is most angry, most aggrieved.

clue.text: Settling for a home beside the : heath

indicators.note: beside means the two pieces stand next to each other in the answer

parts.note: a bird's nest is its home
ling is common heather, a heath plant

explanation.surface: Moving to a house next to the open moorland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ling is the heather that covers British moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestling down means snuggling in and getting comfortable, so it is settling.

clue.text: At no time disturbing 8

indicators.note: disturbing means thrown out of order, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: 8 points to the solution of clue 8 down, whose letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that never stops unsettling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbing' rearranges the letters of the solution to 8 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Never means on no occasion whatever.

clue.text: A woman reading articles in French, Italian, and English

parts.note: le is the French definite article
il is the Italian definite article
a is the English indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman reads grammar points in three languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reading' is a link word; one word for 'the' or 'a' comes from each language.
explanation.definitionFit: Leila is a female given name, so a woman.

clue.text: Pasta or pate?

explanation.surface: A teasing question about whether something is spaghetti or a head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pate' looks like the meat paste, but without its accent it is the old word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A long strip of pasta made from flour and egg; and informally one's head, as in 'use your loaf'.

clue.text: Forms filled up by churchgoers

parts.note: reads as paperwork filled in, but forms are long benches, seats in a church

explanation.walkthrough: A form is an old word for a backless bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Long wooden benches in a church on which the congregation sits.

clue.text: Few signify, that's clear

parts.note: a few is taken as a small number, five, Roman V
to signify is to indicate

explanation.surface: Only a handful of things matter, and that is plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb, as in clearing someone's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate someone is to clear them of blame or suspicion.

clue.text: Better scholar turning tail

indicators.note: turning means the scholar's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar
the tail is the end

explanation.surface: A superior student who turns his back and runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes AM from MA.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend something is to improve or correct it, making it better.

clue.text: Let out again — free

explanation.surface: A property rented once more, and a prisoner set loose.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition splits the word as re-lease: to lease out again.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-lease a flat is to rent it out once more; to release a captive is to set them at liberty.

clue.text: There's a form about the trainee's protection

indicators.note: a form of the letters, turned about, means they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
L, the learner plate, marks a trainee

explanation.surface: A bench stands near the apprentice, giving him cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' tempts as a bench or a hare's lair, but 'a form about' rearranges THERES with L, the learner driver's plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter is cover from weather or danger, so it gives protection.
